analysis:
Examined all supplied source, patches and mode metadata against the canonical index and selected T-041 detail. Desktop (head 24–26), contribution-policy (13–15), landing and nightly-package (17–19) changes cancel superseded runs within workflow/PR-or-ref groups. Permissions, pinned actions, signature validation and build commands remain unchanged; cancellation does not visibly bypass a gate or cross PR boundaries.
Provider-plan.yml adds default-true run_tests (16–19), suppresses classification/lookup when disabled (58, 66), gates GPU lanes by event/label (144–154, 205–207), and removes build routing for previously tested pushes (202–203). These are CI selection changes, not observed serving-authorization or encryption changes. Integration must reconcile callers and provider-tests.yml job conditions with the new outputs and zero-count build lanes. Also verify scripts/ci-tested-tree.py evidence handling: SELECTED still excludes GPU coverage (109), so an earlier successful run without GPU tests could potentially suppress a later labeled run. Supplied evidence does not establish the lookup's acceptance contract or a security-critical GPU requirement, so this is not a finding.
Provider-release-cache.yml's patch changes push warming to daily scheduling, enables cancellation, and adds an API-based warm gate (head 46–177). It requires both warm jobs to have succeeded, bounds prior evidence to six days, checks renamed paths, and warms on API errors or large/divergent comparisons. The pattern list omits scripts formerly included by the push trigger; this can delay warming but is not evidence of unsafe release reuse. BASE 101–125 identifies unsigned preparation and handoff validation, not durable signed-build approval. Integration should verify that reduced warming/test selection cannot substitute for release validation or qualification (A-017, T-054). No direct change to prompt confidentiality, T-041 cache isolation, credentials, billing, privileged helpers or serving grants is visible. Caller, lookup and release-cache consumer contracts remain material coverage limits, not proven regressions.
